title: Brake Change Interval Below Contract Assumption on Short-Sector Operation
abstract: Pyrenean Air reports brake changes falling due at roughly two thirds of the interval assumed in its support contract, driven by a high proportion of short sectors, and asks for a longer-life heat stack.

sections.request: We bought into a support contract built on an assumed brake life and we are not getting anywhere near it. Our network has moved towards shorter sectors and higher frequency over the last four years, and the brakes are now the single biggest driver of unscheduled wheel and brake visits on the fleet. We are changing units at about two thirds of the life the contract assumed. The wear is even, there is nothing wrong with the units, they are simply being worked harder than the original assumption. We are asking whether there is a longer-life brake available for this aircraft, or whether one can be made available, because our alternative is to renegotiate the contract and neither of us wants that.
sections.background: Our fleet flew an average sector length of 3.9 hours in 2021 and 2.6 hours in 2025. Over the same period the mean brake change interval fell from 1 480 to 1 010 landings. Our wheel and brake shop reports uniform wear with no evidence of dragging, uneven pressure or control anomalies, and the brake control units have not been implicated in any removal. We have already embodied the current control unit standard across the fleet.
sections.expected_outcome: A brake assembly with a heat stack that gives at least the originally assumed life at our present sector length, interchangeable on the aircraft with the units we already have, and available as a spares reference so we can introduce it as units come due rather than as a fleet campaign.

type_data.business_justification: Brake change interval 32 per cent below the assumption underwriting a component support contract, with a direct annual cost exposure the operator quantifies at 4.2 million euro across seven aircraft.
